solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Copper, perhaps, to follow soldiers in TV western

parts.note: to trace someone is to follow their trail

indicators.note: the men go inside the reversed television word
in an across clue a western direction is right to left, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: telly or tele is informal for television
men is a common crossword word for soldiers

explanation.surface: A policeman trailing troops through a cowboy programme on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' poses as a policeman, but it is the metal. TELE reversed by 'western' gives ELET, and MEN goes 'in' it: ELEMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper is an example of a mineral the body needs only in minute amounts.

clue.text: Craft raised skill on West Bank, mostly viewed from the south

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word turns it upside down, reading bottom to top

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of conversation

indicators.note: seen from below in a down entry, the word reads upwards
mostly means all but the final letter

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on

explanation.surface: Political geography: a skill raised in the West Bank, seen from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' is the verb (bank on = rely). RELY 'mostly' is REL, which turns into LER when 'viewed from the south'; ART 'raised' gives TRA.
explanation.definitionFit: A craft is any vessel, and a fishing boat that drags a net is one such vessel.

clue.text: Tapestry mounted in disarray

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounted means going upwards, so the letters are read in reverse
the letters sit inside the word disarray

explanation.surface: A wall hanging that has been put up in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: SARRA sits 'in' disarray, and 'mounted' turns it to read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Arras was a French town famed for its woven wall hangings, and its name became a synonym for them.

clue.text: Missing introduction, discourage new friend forever

indicators.note: missing its introduction means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: to deter is to discourage
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: Someone without an introduction putting off a new friend for good.
explanation.walkthrough: DETER 'missing introduction' gives ETER.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean for all time, without end.

clue.text: Prostrate, face up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a dial is the face of a clock

explanation.surface: Lying flat on the ground, face upward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Face up' reads as a lying position, but 'face' is DIAL and 'up' turns it over.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid low or laid out means lying flat, the past participle sense of prostrate.

clue.text: Grow vegetable

definitions.meaning: to grow or spread very rapidly
an edible fungus eaten as a vegetable

explanation.surface: An instruction to cultivate greens.
explanation.definitionFit: The fungus is eaten as a vegetable, and the verb means to expand rapidly, as such fungi appear overnight.

clue.text: Primarily run into debt and navigate around rock bottom

indicators.note: turning around means the picked letters are read in reverse
primarily picks the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Getting into debt and steering a way out of financial rock bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: The initials RIDAN, read 'around', give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The point directly beneath an observer gives the figurative sense of the lowest point.

clue.text: Not all of Wings I spotted in New Orleans

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone saying they caught sight of a band in a Louisiana city, perhaps Paul McCartney's Wings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Orleans' reads as the city, but 'New' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: These hinged flaps form only part of an aircraft's wings, so they are not all of them.

clue.text: Fused magazine's front cover let out by its boss?

indicators.note: the front of the magazine gives its opening letter
let out suggests the letters of let are put out of order

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the boss of a magazine

explanation.surface: A magazine's front cover blown up by its furious editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges LET into ELT.
explanation.definitionFit: Metals melted together are joined into one, which is what fused means.

clue.text: Hot-headed Einstein, say, having arrived before Nobel laureate

indicators.note: the arrival comes before the rest

parts.note: ARR is the timetable abbreviation for arrival or arrived

indicators.note: headed by H means the first letter is replaced

parts.note: Einstein is a classic example of a genius
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

explanation.surface: An impetuous Einstein turned up ahead of a Nobel prizewinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot-headed' looks like a description of Einstein, but GENIUS is 'headed' by H in place of G.
explanation.definitionFit: Svante Arrhenius, Swedish chemist, won the Nobel Prize for Chemistry in 1903.

clue.text: Push end of finger into joint

indicators.note: the letter goes into the word for a bar

parts.note: a dive is a seedy bar or joint

indicators.note: the end of finger is its last letter

explanation.surface: Jamming the tip of a finger into a body joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' is a seedy bar (DIVE), not a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive is to propel or push forward, as one drives cattle.

clue.text: Failing to keep record about crime

indicators.note: the record goes about, round, the crime

parts.note: a log is a written record
sin is a wrongdoing or crime

explanation.surface: Not managing to keep a record of an offence.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'Failing to keep', not 'Failing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Failing to keep something is mislaying it, the present participle of lose.

clue.text: Lewd game in Pinter novel

indicators.note: the game's letters go inside the reworked playwright's name
novel means new, so the letters are given a new order

parts.note: RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: A smutty game in a novel by Harold Pinter.
explanation.walkthrough: Pinter, a British playwright, wrote only one novel, but 'novel' is the anagram signal on PINTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe an excessive, unhealthy interest in sexual matters.

clue.text: Blue rinse is, at first sight, obvious

indicators.note: the first letters of the two words are what is seen first

parts.note: a bald statement is plain and obvious

explanation.surface: A blue hair rinse is plain to see straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue rinse' is a hair tint, but 'Blue' is the definition, meaning smutty.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue jokes are coarse and vulgar, which is what ribald describes.

clue.text: VIP turning up whenever first-rate landlord appears

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up reverses the word to read upwards

parts.note: a nob is a toff or bigwig
if can mean whenever, as in if it rains, I stay in
ace means excellent

explanation.surface: A dignitary showing up wherever a top innkeeper is found.
explanation.walkthrough: Boniface is the jovial innkeeper in Farquhar's 1707 comedy The Beaux' Stratagem, and his name came to mean any innkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: A literary innkeeper's name became a byword for any publican, i.e. a pub landlord.

clue.text: Beatnik clutching old reference book cried

indicators.note: the bohemian word holds the letter inside it

parts.note: boho is short for bohemian, a beatnik type
the OED is the Oxford English Dictionary

explanation.surface: A hippie clinging to an antique dictionary broke down in tears.
explanation.walkthrough: BOHO 'clutching' O gives BOOHO, then OED.
explanation.definitionFit: To boo-hoo is to sob noisily, an imitation of loud weeping.

clue.text: One repeatedly cutting tatty cheaper little rug?

indicators.note: tatty means shabby and messy, so the letters are jumbled
repeatedly means the single one is taken more than once, here twice over

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone keeps trimming a scruffy, cut-price small carpet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' suggests insertion, but the two ones simply join the pool that 'tatty' rearranges. 'Rug' is slang for a toupee.
explanation.definitionFit: Rug is slang for a toupee, and this false hair is a partial wig covering a bald patch.

clue.text: One who can't decide where to cross?

definitions.text: One who can't decide where to cross?

parts.words: One who can't decide where to cross?
parts.note: an undecided survey respondent, and also the box on a questionnaire where such a person puts a cross

explanation.surface: A pedestrian unable to choose where to cross the road.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross is a mark on a voting or survey form, not a street crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: An undecided opinion-poll respondent, and the tick-box on a form for that response.

clue.text: Fantastic sonnet cut by extremely nasty old poet

indicators.note: the jumbled word is cut open by the two letters
fantastic suggests the letters are rearranged fancifully
the extremes are the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A wonderful sonnet slashed by a very unpleasant old versifier.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred, Lord Tennyson was the Victorian Poet Laureate.

clue.text: Trunk call reservation initially restricted by levy

indicators.note: the levy word confines the other letters inside it

parts.note: a tax is a levy
ho is a call to attract attention

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter

explanation.surface: A long-distance phone call booking constrained by a charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trunk call' was an old British phrase for a long-distance phone call, but 'Trunk' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The thorax is the chest, the part of the torso between neck and abdomen.

clue.text: Puzzle jerk with proverb

parts.note: a jig is a jerky up-and-down movement
a saw is an old saying or proverb

explanation.surface: A fool with a wise saying is a mystery.
explanation.definitionFit: A jigsaw is a picture puzzle of interlocking pieces.

clue.text: Lazy attempt to undermine Labour

indicators.note: in a down clue, the attempt goes under the labour word

parts.note: work is labour
a shy is a try, as at a coconut shy

explanation.surface: An idle bid to sabotage the Labour Party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the UK political party, but it means work.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone averse to effort is idle, which is the sense of lazy.

clue.text: Very loud poet is playing around on unfamiliar tracks

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the music marking
playing means the letters are toyed with and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
FF is fortissimo, the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: A noisy poet larking about on routes he doesn't know.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very loud' is the musical marking fortissimo; 'playing' scrambles the poet and is, which then go 'around' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Skiing off-piste is going away from prepared runs, onto tracks one does not know.

clue.text: Stroke, cut wildly, is making the boundary

indicators.note: the word is forms the boundary around the other letters
wildly means the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A cricket shot, slashed wildly, reaches the boundary.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is cricket, where the boundary is the edge of the field, but here 'making the boundary' means the word is encloses the jumbled cut.
explanation.definitionFit: An ictus is a medical stroke or seizure, and also the stress beat in verse.

clue.text: Noise made by Far-Eastern boat entering old city

indicators.note: the boat goes into the city name

parts.note: Ur is the ancient Sumerian city
a proa is a Malay sailing boat

explanation.surface: The din of an Oriental vessel arriving at an ancient port.
explanation.walkthrough: A proa is a Malay outrigger sailing boat.
explanation.definitionFit: An uproar is a loud commotion or tumult.

clue.text: Crew possibly caught in boatyard, dropping the odds

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the even letters
removing the odd-placed letters leaves the even ones

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A crew, perhaps, nabbed in a boatyard, leaving behind the long shots.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of boatyard are OTAD; C goes 'in' after the O.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowing crew can be eight oarsmen, and an octad is a group of eight.

clue.text: Turn using unexpected good fortune, avoiding defeat

indicators.note: avoiding means the defeat word is left out

parts.note: a windfall is an unexpected gain
a fall is a defeat, as the fall of a city

explanation.surface: Changing course with a lucky break and so not losing.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind a handle or a clock is to turn it.

clue.text: Tie in some races

definitions.meaning: a broad neck scarf worn formally
the Royal meeting at the Berkshire racecourse

explanation.surface: A draw in a few of the races.
explanation.definitionFit: The cravat-like neckwear takes its name from the racecourse where it was worn at the races.

clue.text: Dish — note cook sees to it

indicators.note: to cook figures is to falsify them, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A meal is noted down, and the chef handles it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cook' reads as the chef, but it is the anagram signal on SEES TO IT.
explanation.definitionFit: These are small round boneless cuts of meat, served as a dish.

clue.text: Quiet ways ended in turmoil after a fast start

indicators.note: the rest comes after the letter a

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet

indicators.note: turmoil means the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Peaceful roads came to an end in chaos after a quick getaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in turmoil' rearranges WAYS ENDED into WEDNESDAY.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the first day of Lent, the start of a period of fasting.
